# A complete midpoint-star gauge certificate can miss the target

This is an exact obstruction to a particular **lower certificate**, not to mixed-integer depth. Sections 1--4 use an actual convex body, all of its source fibers, and optimize the certificate over **every point** of its central fiber, including its own centroid and all reflected-pair midpoint centroids. Section 7 proves the same upper bound for the corresponding certificate at **every integer anchor and every actual source point**. The original body nevertheless satisfies the OC target by an explicit independent all-cap estimate in Section 5.

The certificate is the one proved in **candidate af36a5fc25ebff84**: align smaller endpoint copies at a chosen point, pay their paired-source bound, and sum over disjoint reflected pairs. Here the exact ordinary depth of the own fiber is used, so replacing a crude own-fiber estimate cannot repair this example.

## 1. The actual 33-fiber body

Let \(d=4\), let

\[
T=\{X\in\mathbb R^4:X_i\ge0,\ \sum_iX_i\le1\},
\qquad V=|T|=\frac1{24},
\qquad g=(1/5,1/5,1/5,1/5).
\]

Put \(K=T-g\), \(v=-g\), and

\[
C=\left\{(z,X)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^4:
 |z|\le16,\quad X_i\ge0,\quad \sum_iX_i+\frac{|z|}{17}\le1\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]

It is a full-dimensional compact convex polytope. Its integer bases are exactly \(-16,\ldots,16\), and every fiber has positive volume:

\[
C_k=r_kT,\qquad r_k=1-\frac{|k|}{17}.
\tag{2}
\]

After the single common translation \(x=X-g\), its fibers are

\[
K_k=c_k+r_kK,\qquad c_k=\frac{|k|}{17}v.
\tag{3}
\]

On each side of zero both the radii and centers interpolate affinely, so \(C\) is also exactly the convex hull of its integer fibers. No unsampled real vertex or lower-dimensional fiber is needed.

At base zero the own fiber is \(K\), its centroid is zero, and the sixteen disjoint pairs are \((-k,k)\), \(1\le k\le16\). Each pair has radius \(r_k\) and midpoint centroid \(m_k=(k/17)v\). Actual convexity gives \(m_k+r_kK\subseteq K\).

The total source mass is

\[
\frac MV
=1+2\sum_{k=1}^{16}(1-k/17)^4
=\frac{571217}{83521}
=\frac{33601}{4913}.
\tag{4}
\]

## 2. The precise certificate being tested

For \(y\in K\), let

\[
p_K(y)=\inf_{H\ni y}|K\cap H|
\]

be the exact ordinary absolute depth of the central fiber. Write
\(\gamma_K\) for its nonsymmetric gauge. Define

\[
\mathcal L(y)
=p_K(y)+2\Gamma_4V
\sum_{k=1}^{16}
\left[r_k-\gamma_K(y-m_k)\right]_+^4.
\tag{5}
\]

For every actual closed cap through or containing \((0,y)\), its central contribution is at least \(p_K(y)\), and the two-copy bound transferred to \(y\) pays the \(k\)-th summand. Thus

\[
A_\mu(0,y)\ge\mathcal L(y).
\tag{6}
\]

The pair bound used here is exact at each pair's own midpoint:
\(\Phi_4(r_k,r_k)V=2\Gamma_4r_k^4V\). The subsequent gauge transfer is the step being tested. There are no omitted integer fibers in (5).

We prove the exact value

\[
\boxed{
\max_{y\in K}\mathcal L(y)
=\Gamma_4V\,\frac{282546}{83521}
<\frac{\Gamma_4M}{2}.
}
\tag{7}
\]

The gap is exactly

\[
\frac{\Gamma_4M}{2}-\max_{y\in K}\mathcal L(y)
=\Gamma_4V\,\frac{6125}{167042}>0.
\tag{8}
\]

This tests more than the finitely many natural midpoint candidates.

## 3. Reduction of every candidate to the vertex-centroid axis

The simplex \(K\), every \(m_k\), and the gauge are invariant under permutations of the four continuous coordinates. Average a candidate \(y\) over these permutations:

\[
\bar y=\left(\frac{\sum_i y_i}{4},\ldots,
             \frac{\sum_i y_i}{4}\right)=t v,
\qquad -\frac14\le t\le1.
\]

Convexity and permutation invariance of the gauge give, simultaneously for all pairs,

\[
\gamma_K(\bar y-m_k)\le\gamma_K(y-m_k).
\tag{9}
\]

When \(0\le t\le1\), the barycentric coordinate of vertex \(v\) is
\(\lambda_0(y)=1/5-\sum_i y_i=(1+4t)/5\).
The vertex cap through \(y\) therefore has volume

\[
V(1-\lambda_0(y))^4
=\Gamma_4V(1-t)^4.
\]

Consequently \(p_K(y)\le\Gamma_4V(1-t)^4\). At \(t v\) this is exact: the centered copy
\(tv+(1-t)K\subseteq K\) supplies the matching lower bound by ordinary Grünbaum. Combining this with (9) proves

\[
\mathcal L(y)\le\mathcal L(tv)\qquad(0\le t\le1).
\tag{10}
\]

When \(t<0\), use \(p_K(y)\le\Gamma_4V\). To justify this elementary simplex bound, at least one of its five barycentric coordinates is at least \(1/5\); the corresponding vertex cap has volume at most \((4/5)^4V\). Moreover

\[
\gamma_K((t-k/17)v)=4(k/17-t)
\ge4k/17=\gamma_K(-m_k).
\]

Together with (9), this implies \(\mathcal L(y)\le\mathcal L(0)\).
It remains only to maximize (5) on \(tv\), \(0\le t\le1\).

Along this line \(\gamma_K(av)=a\) for \(a\ge0\) and
\(\gamma_K(av)=-4a\) for \(a\le0\). Hence

\[
\frac{\mathcal L(tv)}{\Gamma_4V}
=(1-t)^4+
2\sum_{k=1}^{16}
\begin{cases}
(1-t)^4,&k/17\le t,\\
[1-5k/17+4t]_+^4,&k/17\ge t.
\end{cases}
\tag{11}
\]

Each expression agrees at its junction \(t=k/17\).

## 4. A finite exact maximum certificate

On each interval \([j/17,(j+1)/17]\), every term in (11) is either
\((1-t)^4\) or the fourth power of the positive part of an affine function. Each is convex on that interval. A convex function on a compact interval attains a maximum at an endpoint. Thus the maximum occurs at \(t=j/17\), \(j=0,\ldots,17\).

For \(j\le16\), multiply (11) by \(17^4=83521\). Its exact numerator is

\[
C_j=(2j+1)(17-j)^4+
2\sum_{k=j+1}^{16}[17-5k+4j]_+^4.
\tag{12}
\]

The values are:

| \(j\) | \(C_j\) |
|---:|---:|
|0|129827|
|1|228484|
|2|274375|
|3|282546|
|4|265403|
|5|232930|
|6|192927|
|7|151250|
|8|112049|
|9|77986|
|10|50453|
|11|29810|
|12|15625|
|13|6912|
|14|2349|
|15|496|
|16|33|
|17|0|

The largest entry is \(C_3=282546\), proving the equality in (7).
Finally \(571217-2(282546)=6125\), proving (8). In particular the own centroid \(t=0\), all sixteen pair midpoints \(t=k/17\), and every other actual central-fiber point have this certificate strictly below the target.

## 5. Independent explicit OC safety of the original body

Scale only the base coordinate by \(u=z/17\), and write \(h=1/17\). The transformed body is

\[
Q=\{(u,X):|u|\le16/17,\ X\in(1-|u|)T\},
\]

sampled on \(h\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^4\). Its ordinary five-dimensional volume is

\[
|Q|=WV,\qquad
W=2\int_0^{16/17}(1-u)^4\,du
=\frac25(1-h^5)=\frac{2839712}{7099285}.
\tag{13}
\]

Its ordinary centroid has base coordinate zero and continuous coordinates

\[
\bar X_i=\frac16\,\frac{1-h^6}{1-h^5}\qquad(1\le i\le4).
\tag{14}
\]

This is an actual point of the sampled central fiber. Ordinary Grünbaum in dimension five gives volume at least \(\Gamma_5WV\) for every containing cap of \(Q\).

The all-cap one-fine-coordinate discrepancy theorem in
**candidate f525b2b4bb53c54e**
applies with maximal four-dimensional fiber volume \(V\). It gives, for every such closed cap, sampled \(h\)-weighted mass at least

\[
V(\Gamma_5W-h).
\tag{15}
\]

This includes pure base-normal caps and full boundary fibers; no boundary sample is discarded. The exact total sampled \(h\)-weighted mass is

\[
hM=\frac{33601}{83521}V.
\]

Thus the actual normalized depth at (14) is at least

\[
\frac{\Gamma_5W-h}{hM/V}
=\frac{35167522}{138805731}
>\frac{128}{625}=\frac{\Gamma_4}{2}.
\tag{16}
\]

The exact positive difference before normalization is

\[
\Gamma_5W-h-\frac{\Gamma_4}{2}\frac{hM}{V}
=\frac{4212567682}{215640781875}>0.
\tag{17}
\]

This is a direct lower bound for all original cap directions, because base scaling is invertible and preserves halfspaces. It establishes safety without an OC assumption or a numerical depth screen.

## 6. Scope

The source radii and pair centroids vary with \(k\), all fibers are homothetic actual simplices, and the reflected pairs exhaust the source outside the central fiber. The countercertificate shows that the transferred paired-tail bounds cannot simply be optimized over candidate points and summed to obtain the target, even after replacing the own-fiber term by its exact ordinary depth.

Section 7 also excludes repairing this precise certificate just by changing the integer anchor. It does not disprove a stronger endpoint estimate, a coupled choice of cap normals, or other contributions from unpaired sources at a noncentral anchor. In particular (16) proves that the original body has a much better all-cap lower bound than this particular gauge certificate records.

The exact verifier **../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_complete_midpoint_star_gauge_shortfall.py** checks the finite maximum table, total mass and gap, the sampling constants, and the independent all-cap safety comparison. Equations (9)--(12) justify why that finite arithmetic certifies the full continuum of central-fiber candidates.

## 7. The same obstruction at every integer anchor

For each integer \(k\in[-16,16]\), use **every available reflected pair** about \(k\), count the exact ordinary depth \(p_{K_k}(y)\) of its own fiber, and use the proved unequal-scale \(\Phi_d\) and exact displacement gauge for each pair. Denote this certificate by

\[
\mathcal L_k(y)=p_{K_k}(y)+
V\sum_{\substack{h\ge1\\k-h,k+h\in[-16,16]}}
\left[1-\frac{\gamma_K(y-m_{k,h})}{\rho_{k,h}}\right]_+^4
\Phi_4(r_{k-h},r_{k+h}),\qquad y\in K_k.
\tag{18}
\]

The midpoint radius and centroid are
\(\rho_{k,h}=(r_{k-h}+r_{k+h})/2\) and
\(m_{k,h}=(c_{k-h}+c_{k+h})/2\).
This is a valid all-cap lower bound at the actual point \((k,y)\).
At noncentral anchors the available reflected pairs do not exhaust all the other source fibers; those unpaired fibers receive no automatic contribution in (18).

We prove the exact global certificate maximum

\[
\boxed{
\max_{\substack{k\in[-16,16]\cap\mathbb Z\\y\in K_k}}\mathcal L_k(y)
=\Gamma_4V\,\frac{282546}{83521}
<\frac{\Gamma_4M}{2}.
}
\tag{19}
\]

First record a general upper comparison for the proved lower-bound function:

\[
\Phi_d(r,s)\le
2\Gamma_d\left(\frac{r+s}{2}\right)^d
\qquad(r,s>0,\ d\ge1).
\tag{20}
\]

This is an inequality about \(\Phi_d\), not a lower bound for actual paired caps by the right side, which is false in general. For \(d=1\), it is just \(\min(r,s)\le(r+s)/2\). For \(d\ge2\), assume \(r\le s\), and put \(c=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}=2^{1/d}d/(d+1)\). In particular \(c\ge2/(d+1)\). In the interpolation regime,

\[
rc+\frac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c)
\le rc+\frac{s-r}{2}c
=c\frac{r+s}{2},
\]

because \(2(1-c)\le(d-1)c\). In the plateau regime \(s\ge dr\),
\[
c(r+s)/2\ge c(d+1)r/2\ge r.
\]
These prove (20) in both cases.

Reflection in the base sends \(k\) to \(-k\) without changing any continuous fiber, so assume \(0\le k\le16\), and put \(a=1/17\).
The available pair indices are \(1\le h\le16-k\). Their exact data are

\[
\rho_{k,h}=1-a\max(k,h),\qquad
m_{k,h}=a\max(k,h)v.
\tag{21}
\]

All pair centroids therefore lie on the vertex ray at or beyond the own centroid \(c_k=akv\).

As in Section 3, average the four coordinates of \(y\) to obtain
\(\bar y=xv\); this can only decrease every gauge appearing in (18).
If \(x<ak\), the simplex bound
\[
p_{K_k}(y)\le\Gamma_4Vr_k^4=p_{K_k}(c_k)
\]
and the gauge formula on the negative vertex ray show that replacing \(\bar y\) by \(c_k\) can only increase the certificate. Thus it suffices to consider \(ak\le x\le1\). In that range the same vertex-cap calculation as before gives

\[
p_{K_k}(y)\le\Gamma_4V(1-x)^4
=p_{K_k}(xv).
\tag{22}
\]

For such an axis candidate, (20) bounds the pair term in (18) by

\[
2\Gamma_4V
\left[\rho_{k,h}-\gamma_K(xv-m_{k,h})\right]_+^4.
\tag{23}
\]

If \(h>k\), its radius and midpoint in (21) are exactly those of central pair \(h\), so (23) is precisely the central \(h\)-term at \(xv\). If \(h\le k\), then \(x\ge ak\ge ah\), and both the noncentral expression in (23) and the central \(h\)-term equal
\[
2\Gamma_4V(1-x)^4.
\]

Together with (22), this proves termwise

\[
\mathcal L_k(y)\le\mathcal L_0(xv)
\]

after the permitted averaging and, when necessary, replacement by \(c_k\). The central certificate includes all \(h=1,\ldots,16\), while the noncentral sum stops at \(16-k\); every omitted central term is nonnegative.
Equation (7) now proves the upper bound in (19). Equality is already attained at the central point \(k=0,\ y=(3/17)v\).

Thus all choices of integer anchor, all original continuous candidate points, the exact own-fiber depth, the exact gauge rather than its radius-only relaxation, and all available reflected pairs still leave the shortfall (8). The independent actual-depth bound (16) remains unchanged.
